review_scope: Only the specified original physical pages were independently checked; neither entire paper was reviewed.

papers.title: Deep learning perturbation models can outperform baselines on calibrated metrics
Spurious correlation inflates performance in single-cell perturbation prediction

supported_design_changes: Report complementary metric families and test sensitivity to data quality.
Evaluate combinatorial prediction beyond a single sparsely covered dataset.
Compare shared-control and independently split-control estimates with repeated splits.
corrections: Interpolated duplicate accesses held-out data: use it only for evaluation calibration or an upper-bound reference, separated from predictors and tuning.
PCA-linear and additive predictors are baselines, not automatically positive controls.
Control splitting does not guarantee correct rankings on a new dataset; attenuation and variability require validation.
A nonzero null estimate does not by itself establish leakage.
The shared-control correction does not automatically apply to every Pearson delta definition.
Poor calibration in the reported settings does not establish universal MSE or Pearson underestimation.
remaining_work: Read exact metric definitions, Methods, supplementary details and relevant code before fixing the implementation.
Validate rankings, uncertainty and generalization in the intended experimental setting.
Refresh the matching literature search and inspect other key work before making current-frontier or novelty claims.
